sent_to_model:
I need some help writing an email to colleagues about my gas trading figures over Christmas 2000. The price I submitted needs some explanation because the online transactions do not account for all the business we did. I want to account for the $16.00 figure and include the telephone trades behind my estimate. There is also some background about the different holiday schedules and concerns over the Gas Daily posting that needs to be included. I should acknowledge that I overstated the volume slightly through a quick review of the figures, and make clear that this was an oversight.

- Nicor Gas Company took its company holiday December 22nd; most other companies took December 26th.
- Usual reporting method: use the trade price shown by Enron Online.
- Telephone deal: PG&E; $14.00; volume 9,000; NGPL Nicor.
- December 21, 2000 trading activity covered December 22-26, 2000.
- Telephone deal: Nicor Gas Company; $18.16; volume 20,000; Via ANR @ Hampshire.
- Gas Daily’s published figure for December 22-26: $15.70.
- Telephone deal: WPS; GDD; volume 5,000; NGPL Nicor.
- Reported weighted average: $16.00. Online weighted average alone: $15.76.
- Telephone deal: Kaztex; $18.16; volume 4,000; NBPL/Nicor.
- Nicor Gas Company elected to purchase on December 22nd, covering December 23-26.
- Telephone deal: Altrade; GDD +.05; volume 10,000; NGPL Nicor.
- Different holiday arrangements led to trading covering December 22-26.
- Telephone deal: Nicor Gas Company; $12.00; volume 20,000; NGPL Nicor.
- Including business done by telephone, estimated midpoint was $16.00.
- Occasionally substantial telephone volumes affect the price indicated by online transactions.
- Several marketers called about a possible Gas Daily revision; their concern involved the small amount of trading on December 22nd.
- My reported volume was slightly too high because I reviewed it quickly; I did not deliberately submit inaccurate information.
- Colleagues should understand the estimate’s basis and why the holiday trading period attracted attention.
- Acknowledge the volume discrepancy and distinguish the oversight from deliberate misreporting.

(About me: natural gas trader. Length: it should come to roughly 250-400 words.)

must_cover: Explain the reported $16.00 price using both online activity and the telephone trades.
Provide the telephone trade details supporting the estimate.
Describe the holiday schedules and concerns about a possible Gas Daily price revision.
Acknowledge that a cursory review caused the slight volume overstatement, an oversight rather than deliberate misreporting.

reference.kind: a real piece of writing by a real person

source.licence_note: none on the card; the corpus entered the public record via FERC (2003)
